domain_entities.name: DemoSeed
attributes: appliedAt: Date | null (when the seed last ran successfully)

naturalKeys: string[] (identity keys used to detect already-seeded rows — employeeNumber/email, leaveTypeCode, policy leaveTypeCode+effectiveFrom, balance (employeeId,leaveTypeCode,periodStart,periodEnd), request identity)
domain_entities.purpose: Represents the development-only, idempotent demo dataset (one manager, one employee, leave types, policies, a current-period balance per employee, and 2–3 leave requests in different states). It is a seed concept, not a persisted runtime entity; its lifecycle captures whether the dataset has been applied.

domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: A person who can authenticate and request leave. The seed mints one MANAGER and one EMPLOYEE whose managerId links the employee to the manager, with bcrypt password hashes so POST /auth/login succeeds.

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
attributes: code: LeaveTypeCode (annual | sick | emergency | unpaid | maternity | paternity)
domain_entities.purpose: Static catalog of leave categories. The seed inserts the leave types the balance logic needs (at minimum annual, plus any others referenced by seeded policies).

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines entitlement and accrual rules per leave type. The seed inserts ACTIVE policies so the balance logic (openPeriod/getCurrentBalances) can resolve entitlements and accrual periods.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: One employee's entitlement counters for one leave type and one accrual period. The seed creates a balance for the CURRENT accrual period for each seeded employee so GET /balances/me returns data.

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
attributes: status: LeaveStatus (DRAFT | SUBMITTED | APPROVED | REJECTED | CANCELLED)
domain_entities.purpose: An employee's leave application moving through the approval lifecycle. The seed inserts 2–3 requests in different states so the list and detail pages have data to render.

business_rules: Seeded employee password hashes must be minted by the same bcrypt call the auth service verifies with (bcrypt.hash / bcrypt.hashSync with the same cost factor the login path's bcrypt.compare expects), so POST /auth/login succeeds for the demo credentials. Never store or seed a plaintext password. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Employee.passwordHash (seed) appears, not only here]

The seed must be idempotent: running it twice must neither duplicate rows nor fail. Each seeded row is identified by a natural key (employeeNumber/email for employees, code for leave types, leaveTypeCode+effectiveFrom for policies, (employeeId, leaveTypeCode, periodStart, periodEnd) for balances, and a stable identity for leave requests); a re-run detects an already-seeded row and skips it. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever DemoSeed appears, not only here]

All seeded dates are calendar dates in UTC (whole-day UTC midnight instants), consistent with the existing UTC date discipline; no local-timezone or time-of-day components are introduced by the seed. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever DemoSeed dates (hireDate, effectiveFrom, periodStart/periodEnd, startDate/endDate) appears, not only here]

The seeded current-period balance for each employee must be derived using the shared periodContaining(hireDate, accrualPeriodMonths, now) helper (anchored on hireDate), never a hand-written date, so the seeded periodStart/periodEnd match what getCurrentBalances computes at runtime. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance (seed, current accrual period) appears, not only here]

Seeded leave requests must be consistent with the seeded balance counters: a SUBMITTED request contributes its requestedDays to pendingDays, and an APPROVED request contributes its requestedDays to usedDays, so available = entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays reflects the seeded requests. requestedDays must be derived via the shared requestedDays(startDate, endDate) helper (inclusive calendar days), never hand-computed. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest + LeaveBalance (seed consistency) appears, not only here]

The seed is development data only and must never run automatically as part of migrate; it is applied only via an explicit seed command targeting the development environment. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever DemoSeed appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
This feature is a development-only seed + run-script feature; it introduces no new runtime entities, no new lifecycle states, and no changes to existing entity shapes. The domain slice reuses the existing canonical entities (Employee, LeaveType, LeavePolicy, LeaveBalance, LeaveRequest) and their already-reconciled lifecycle states, and adds one seed-only concept (DemoSeed) to capture the idempotency/application lifecycle.

Lifecycle states (all pre-existing, none new — for the chief architect to fold into architectureMdUpdate):
- Employee: ACTIVE | TERMINATED | ON_LEAVE
- LeavePolicy: DRAFT | ACTIVE | SUPERSEDED
- LeaveBalance: OPEN | CLOSED (inferred from periodStart/periodEnd, not stored)
- LeaveRequest: DRAFT | SUBMITTED | APPROVED | REJECTED | CANCELLED
- LeaveType: static catalog, no lifecycle states
- DemoSeed (new, seed-only): UNAPPLIED | APPLIED

Binding business rules (broad scope):
- Seeded password hashes minted by the same bcrypt call the auth service verifies with (never plaintext).
- Seed idempotency via natural keys (employeeNumber/email, code, leaveTypeCode+effectiveFrom, (employeeId,leaveTypeCode,periodStart,periodEnd), and a stable request identity).
- All seeded dates are UTC calendar dates (whole-day UTC midnight).
- Current-period balance derived via shared periodContaining(hireDate, accrualPeriodMonths, now), never hand-written.
- Seeded requests consistent with balance counters (SUBMITTED→pendingDays, APPROVED→usedDays); requestedDays via shared requestedDays helper.
- Seed is development-only and never runs as part of migrate.

Open questions (need human decision):
- LeaveRequest idempotency identity (no natural key; id is a generated UUID).
- Whether the MANAGER also gets a current-period balance.

No persistence, module, or API concerns are specified here — those belong to the data and application architects.

open_questions.question: LeaveRequest has no natural key (id is a generated UUID), so how does the idempotent seed detect an already-seeded leave request to skip it on re-run?
open_questions.impact: Determines the idempotency mechanism for the 2–3 seeded leave requests; without a stable identity the seed would duplicate requests on every run.
candidate_options: Use a deterministic composite key (employeeId + leaveTypeCode + startDate + endDate + status) to detect an existing request
Use a fixed, well-known id string for seeded requests (e.g. 'seed-leave-1')
Delete-and-reinsert seeded requests on each run (upsert by composite key)

open_questions.question: Should the seed create a current-period leave balance for the MANAGER as well as the EMPLOYEE, or only for the EMPLOYEE?
open_questions.impact: Affects whether the manager's GET /balances/me returns data and whether the manager can be used to exercise the full demo flow; the feature text says "a leave balance ... for each employee" which is ambiguous about whether the manager counts.
candidate_options: Create a balance for both the manager and the employee
Create a balance only for the employee (manager is for approval only)
